stack.title: How devlog works
stack.description: devlog is a full-stack project built from scratch: a React SPA, a REST API in Express and a MongoDB database. Here is what is inside and how the parts talk to each other.
stack.flowTitle: What happens when you save a post
stack.flowDescription: Every protected request goes through the same chain of middleware before it reaches the database.

steps.title: fetch("/api/...")
steps.desc: The browser sends the request with an httpOnly cookie. The frontend and the API share one domain, so no CORS is needed.

steps.title: verifyToken
steps.desc: Reads the JWT from the cookie and checks its signature. No valid token means 401.

steps.title: requireAdmin · blockDemo
steps.desc: Checks the role. Only admins can write posts, and the demo account is read-only. Otherwise 403.

steps.title: zod
steps.desc: Validates the request body. Errors come back as codes like TITLE_TOO_SHORT, translated in the UI.

steps.title: Mongoose
steps.desc: The controller saves the post in MongoDB and returns JSON in one consistent shape.

steps.title: React
steps.desc: The UI updates and shows a toast. Session state lives in Redux and is checked against /auth/me on startup.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.desc: Email and password or Google sign-in verified on the server. JWT session in an httpOnly cookie.

admin.title: Admin dashboard
admin.desc: Stats with a six-month chart, a rich-text editor with image upload, and tables for posts, comments and users.

security.title: Security
security.desc: helmet headers, rate-limited sign-in, zod validation and post HTML sanitized with DOMPurify.
